claim: This is the first empirical study examining the robustness of state-of-the-art code models to ambiguous, contradictory, and incomplete task descriptions, applied as whole-prompt perturbations.
stance_target: existence and scope of prior work on prompt-robustness in code generation
scope_conditions: code LLMs, perturbed HumanEval/MBPP-style task descriptions
quoted_support: In this paper, we present the first empirical study examining the robustness of state of the art [code models] ... where task descriptions frequently exhibit ambiguity, incompleteness, or internal contradictions.

claim: Ambiguous, contradictory, and incomplete task descriptions are applied and evaluated at the whole-task level, not decomposed to identify whether ambiguity concentrated on one sub-requirement of a multi-requirement task predicts failure of that specific sub-requirement.
stance_target: granularity gap a per-requirement harness could exploit
quoted_support: task descriptions frequently exhibit ambiguity, incompleteness, or internal contradictions
